questions.question:
D1 — ADMIN-1: Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-oRKiaK on main, reviewing the saved-views plan.
ELI10: gstack skills work best when CLAUDE.md tells Claude which skill to reach for (bugs → /investigate, strategy → /plan-ceo-review, etc). This is a one-time onboarding prompt for this project. Note: we are in plan mode, so if you pick A the CLAUDE.md append and commit happen after plan mode exits, not now.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without routing, you invoke each skill by name manually; with it, a fixture repo gets an extra committed section it may not want.
Recommendation: A because routing makes skill use automatic and the section is small and reversible.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Add routing rules (recommended)
  ✅ Future requests auto-route to the right gstack skill without remembering names
  ✅ One small appended section, plain markdown, easy to delete later
  ❌ Adds a commit to a fixture repo that currently has a single seed commit
B) No thanks, invoke manually
  ✅ Keeps CLAUDE.md exactly as the fixture author wrote it
  ✅ Zero writes to the repo; only a local ~/.gstack config flag is set
  ❌ You must remember and type skill names yourself every time
Net: convenience for future sessions vs keeping the fixture repo untouched.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Auto-routes future requests to the matching gstack skill. ✅ Small reversible markdown section. ❌ Adds a commit to the fixture repo (deferred until plan mode exits).

options.label: No thanks, invoke manually
options.description: ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as the fixture author wrote it. ✅ Only a local config flag is written. ❌ You type skill names yourself every time.

questions.question:
D2 — ADMIN-2: Let gstack search learnings from your other local projects?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-oRKiaK on main, reviewing the saved-views plan.
ELI10: gstack logs small lessons per project (command quirks, pitfalls). Cross-project mode lets this review also read lessons logged in your other repos on this machine. Nothing leaves the machine. Good for solo devs; skip if you juggle client codebases that must stay separate.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Enabled on a multi-client machine could surface a client-specific pattern in the wrong repo; disabled on a solo machine just means fewer prior-learning hits.
Recommendation: A because this is a local machine flag and you appear to be one developer across these repos.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Reviews get smarter faster by reusing lessons from every repo on this machine
  ✅ Stays fully local; a single config flag you can flip back any time
  ❌ A learning from an unrelated codebase could be surfaced where it does not apply
B) Keep learnings project-scoped
  ✅ Hard isolation between codebases; nothing from another repo ever appears here
  ✅ Safest default when you work across multiple clients or employers
  ❌ Each new project starts cold and relearns the same environment quirks
Net: faster compounding vs strict per-repo isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Reuses lessons from all local repos so reviews compound faster. ✅ Local-only flag, reversible. ❌ Unrelated-repo lesson could surface here.

options.label: Keep project-scoped
options.description: ✅ Hard isolation between codebases. ✅ Safest for multi-client work. ❌ Every project starts cold.

questions.question:
D3 — MODE: Which review mode for the saved-views plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-oRKiaK on main; plan adds a saved_views table, CRUD endpoints, and a picker beside task filters.
ELI10: The plan is an added capability on an existing product, roughly 12 changed files (estimate; no code in this checkout). It is right-shaped but leaves three edges undefined: what the list opens on (last view vs default), what happens when a saved filter references a deleted assignee or label, and whether views are personal-only forever or the schema should leave room for team-shared views. The mode decides how hard I push on scope: expand, cherry-pick, hold, or cut.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Expand too far and a two-week pilot feature becomes a quarter of work; hold too tight and the schema ships without room for sharing, forcing a migration later.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because those three edges are cheapest to decide while the migration is being written, and cherry-picking lets you accept or decline each one on its own without inflating the pilot.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
  ✅ Hardens the current scope AND offers each expansion (open-on-last-view, sharing-ready schema, deleted-ref handling) as a separate yes/no
  ✅ Keeps the pilot small while avoiding a schema you regret in six months
  ❌ More decision prompts than HOLD SCOPE; you answer one question per candidate
B) SCOPE EXPANSION
  ✅ Aims at the full ideal: team-shared views, default view per project, deep links, notifications on views
  ✅ Best if saved views are meant to become a platform primitive, not a pilot
  ❌ Turns a two-week pilot into a multi-sprint feature before you know anyone reuses views
C) HOLD SCOPE
  ✅ Maximum rigor on exactly what is written: error paths, tests, observability, no additions
  ✅ Fastest path to an implementable spec for the pilot as scoped
  ❌ The three undefined edges get flagged as risks but not offered as additions; schema may need a later migration for sharing
D) SCOPE REDUCTION
  ✅ Strips to the minimum (e.g. remember last filter, no named views) to test the premise cheapest
  ✅ Lowest cost if you doubt members will bother naming views at all
  ❌ Loses the multi-context use case (switching between named lists) that the goal explicitly names
Net: how much of the six-month shape you want to settle now versus after the pilot proves reuse.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Harden current scope, then a separate yes/no for each of the three undefined edges. ✅ Pilot stays small, schema avoids regret. ❌ More prompts than HOLD.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: ✅ Go for the full ideal: shared views, project defaults, deep links. ✅ Right if views become a platform primitive. ❌ Pilot becomes multi-sprint before reuse is proven.

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: ✅ Max rigor on exactly what is written; fastest to implementable spec. ✅ No additions. ❌ Undefined edges flagged as risks only; sharing may need a later migration.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: ✅ Strip to remember-last-filter to test the premise cheapest. ✅ Lowest cost if naming views is doubtful. ❌ Drops the multi-context case the goal names.
